learning_path:
**Course Recommendations**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX2972 | International Human Rights Law | edx | Foundational knowledge of human rights law |
| 2 | EDX2117 | International Humanitarian Law | edx | Builds on foundational knowledge, focusing on humanitarian law |
| 3 | EDX1241 | International Law | edx | Explores the broader context of international law, including its relationship with human rights and humanitarian law |
| 4 | EDX3160 | Asylum and Refugee Law | edx | Delves into a specific area of human rights law, asylum and refugee law |
| 5 | EDX660 | Child Protection: Children's Rights in Theory and Practice | edx | Applies human rights and humanitarian law to a specific context, child protection |
| 6 | EDX2876 | (English) International Standards on Freedom of Expression and Safety of Journalists | edx | Examines the intersection of human rights and international law in the context of freedom of expression and safety of journalists |
| 7 | EDX2770 | Freedom of Expression and Information in the Time of Globalization: Foundational Course | edx | Provides a foundational understanding of freedom of expression and information in the context of globalization |
| 8 | EDX3071 | International Investment Law | edx | Explores the intersection of human rights and international law in the context of international investment law |
| 9 | EDX2826 | The EU and Human Rights | edx | Examines the relationship between the European Union and human rights law |
| 10 | EDX496 | Contemporary Issues in World Politics | edx | Encourages critical thinking and analysis of complex issues in world politics, including human rights and international law |

**How the path fits together**

This course path provides a comprehensive understanding of human rights and international humanitarian law, starting with foundational knowledge and building towards more complex and nuanced topics. The path covers the full duration requested, with at least one course per period. Each course follows logically from the previous one, with EDX2972 providing foundational knowledge of human rights law, which is built upon in EDX2117 with a focus on humanitarian law. EDX1241 explores the broader context of international law, while EDX3160 and EDX660 delve into specific areas of human rights law, asylum and refugee law, and child protection, respectively. EDX2876 and EDX2770 examine the intersection of human rights and international law in the context of freedom of expression and safety of journalists, and freedom of expression and information in the context of globalization, respectively. EDX3071 explores the intersection of human rights and international law in the context of international investment law, while EDX2826 examines the relationship between the European Union and human rights law. Finally, EDX496 encourages critical thinking and analysis of complex issues in world politics, including human rights and international law.

learning_path:
**Learning Path for Data Science in 6 Months**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 weeks | EDX140 | The Essentials of Data Literacy Online Course | edx | Foundational knowledge of data literacy, including data analysis, visualization, and communication. |
| 2-4 weeks | EDX3425 | Data Science with Python | edx | Develops skills in data science and analysis techniques, including machine learning and statistical learning theory. |
| 4-6 weeks | EDX657 | Data Analytics Basics for Everyone | edx | Introduces data structures, file formats, and data sources, as well as data warehousing and ETL processes. |
| 6 weeks | EDX267 | Programming for Data Science | edx | Focuses on programming concepts, data analysis, and computational thinking. |
| 8-10 weeks | EDX2052 | Introduction to Data Science with Python | edx | Develops hands-on experience with Python programming and coding for modeling, statistics, and storytelling. |
| 10-12 weeks | EDX3032 | R Programming Basics for Data Science | edx | Introduces R programming language and data structures, including vectors, factors, lists, and data frames. |
| 12-14 weeks | EDX2310 | Python Basics for Data Science | edx | Develops skills in Python programming and data analysis, including data visualization and machine learning. |
| 14-16 weeks | EDX575 | Big Data Technology Capstone Project | edx | Applies knowledge of big data technologies to a real-life scenario, including data warehousing, data lakes, and ETL processes. |
| 16 weeks | EDX873 | Analyzing Data with Python | edx | Focuses on data analysis and visualization using Python, including Pandas, NumPy, and SciPy libraries. |

The learning path starts with foundational knowledge of data literacy, followed by development of skills in data science and analysis techniques. The path then introduces data structures, file formats, and data sources, as well as data warehousing and ETL processes. The learner will also develop skills in programming concepts, data analysis, and computational thinking. Finally, the path focuses on hands-on experience with Python programming and coding for modeling, statistics, and storytelling, as well as data visualization and machine learning.
expanded_query: I want to learn data science in 6 months, with a prerequisite level of beginner and a duration of 6 months.

**Learning Path Recommendation**
=====================================

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU4667 | Introduction to Cybersecurity Foundations | Coursera | Foundational knowledge of cybersecurity concepts, networking, and cloud computing. |
| 2 | COU2156 | IT Fundamentals for Cybersecurity Specialization | Coursera | Builds on foundational knowledge, covering networking basics, cybersecurity, and database vulnerabilities. |
| 3 | COU5344 | Cybersecurity Fundamentals Specialization | Coursera | Develops foundational knowledge into a comprehensive understanding of cybersecurity, including computer security incident management and security domains. |
| 4 | COU6211 | Cybersecurity and Its Ten Domains | Coursera | Expands knowledge to cover the ten domains of cybersecurity, including cryptography and information security. |
| 5 | COU3464 | Offensive Hacking Unfolded - Become a Pro Pentester | Coursera | Introduces penetration testing and ethical hacking concepts, building on foundational knowledge. |
| 6 | COU1681 | Cybersecurity Operations Fundamentals Specialization | Coursera | Develops skills in cybersecurity operations, including network security and information security. |
| 7 | COU1293 | Certified Ethical Hacking (v12) Specialization | Coursera | Advances to intermediate-level ethical hacking, covering cryptography, network security, and penetration testing. |
| 8 | COU3642 | The Complete Pentesting and Privilege Escalation Course | Coursera | Focuses on advanced pentesting and privilege escalation techniques, building on intermediate-level knowledge. |
| 9 | COU5900 | Introduction to Network Security | Coursera | Introduces network security concepts, including network architecture and cybersecurity. |
| 10 | COU1476 | Preparing for Your Professional Cloud Network Engineer Journey | Coursera | Develops advanced skills in cloud network engineering, including load balancing and network security. |

**Path Explanation**
-------------------

This learning path is designed to progress from foundational knowledge of cybersecurity concepts to advanced skills in penetration testing and cloud network engineering. The path starts with an introduction to cybersecurity foundations, followed by a specialization in IT fundamentals, which covers networking basics and cybersecurity. The next step is a comprehensive understanding of cybersecurity, including computer security incident management and security domains. The path then expands to cover the ten domains of cybersecurity, including cryptography and information security. The learner is then introduced to penetration testing and ethical hacking concepts, followed by a specialization in cybersecurity operations. The path advances to intermediate-level ethical hacking, covering cryptography, network security, and penetration testing. The learner is then focused on advanced pentesting and privilege escalation techniques. Finally, the path concludes with an introduction to network security concepts and advanced skills in cloud network engineering.

This path covers the full duration of the learner's request, with at least one course per period. The courses are chosen to build on each other, progressing from foundational to advanced knowledge. The path prioritizes hands-on exercises, simulations, and real-world projects to help the learner apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios.

2        | COU1870   | Cloud Computing Primer: Platform as a Service (PaaS) | Coursera | In-depth knowledge of cloud platforms and PaaS

4        | COU2175   | Cloud Fundamentals | Coursera | Foundational knowledge of cloud computing deployment models and service providers
5        | COU4841   | Palo Alto Networks Cloud Security Fundamentals | Coursera | Advanced knowledge of cloud security, including malware and denial-of-service attack (DoS) prevention
5        | COU4922   | Intro to Managing Resources Using Infrastructure-as-Code | Coursera | Practical skills in infrastructure-as-code management

---------------------------

This learning path is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of cloud computing infrastructure and DevOps deployment, progressing from foundational to advanced knowledge. The first period covers the basics of cloud computing and DevOps, while the second period delves deeper into cloud platforms and PaaS. The third period focuses on practical skills in DevOps deployment on AWS, including continuous integration and delivery. The fourth period covers advanced knowledge of DevOps on AWS, including continuous integration and delivery, and preparation for Google Cloud certification. The final period emphasizes cloud security and infrastructure-as-code management. Each course builds on the previous one, providing a cohesive and structured learning experience.

learning_path:
**Learning Path for Discrete Mathematics and Logic**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX1479 | How to Code: Simple Data | edx | Introduces the basics of data representation and programming concepts |
| 2 | EDX874 | Computer Vision for Embedded Systems | edx | Builds on the previous course by introducing computer vision concepts |
| 3 | EDX1758 | Graph Algorithms | edx | Explores graph algorithms and their applications in computer science |
| 4 | EDX1482 | Optimization: principles and algorithms - Network and discrete optimization | edx | Covers optimization techniques and their applications in computer science |
| 5 | EDX1629 | C Programming: Advanced Data Types | edx | Focuses on advanced data types and programming concepts in C |
| 6 | EDX2780 | Cyber Security Basics: A Hands-on Approach | edx | Introduces the basics of cyber security and its applications in computer science |
| 7 | EDX1079 | Digital Design | edx | Covers digital design concepts and their applications in computer science |
| 8 | EDX1626 | C Programming: Modular Programming and Memory Management | edx | Explores modular programming and memory management concepts in C |
| 9 | EDX590 | Google AI for Anyone | edx | Introduces machine learning and AI concepts and their applications in computer science |
| 10 | EDX2093 | MATLAB Essentials | edx | Covers the basics of MATLAB programming and its applications in computer science |

**Learning Path for Photography and Visual Design**
==============================================

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU4519 | Photography Capstone Project | Coursera | This course provides a foundation in photography and visual design, covering the basics of light, composition, and visual elements. |
| 2 | COU3003 | Design Fundamentals | Coursera | Building on the previous course, this one covers the fundamentals of visual design, including typography, color theory, and visual storytelling. |
| 3 | COU4668 | Graphic Design Fundamentals | Coursera | This course introduces the basics of graphic design, including color schemes, visual storytelling, and visual design principles. |
| 4 | COU5436 | Image Editing | Coursera | With a solid foundation in graphic design, this course teaches image editing skills using Adobe Photoshop. |
| 5 | COU4519 | Photography Capstone Project | Coursera | This course provides an opportunity to apply the skills learned in the previous courses to a real-world project, with feedback and guidance. |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path is designed to take a complete beginner in photography and visual design from the basics to a more advanced level. The first course, Photography Capstone Project, provides a foundation in photography and visual design, covering the basics of light, composition, and visual elements. The second course, Design Fundamentals, builds on this foundation, covering the fundamentals of visual design, including typography, color theory, and visual storytelling. The third course, Graphic Design Fundamentals, introduces the basics of graphic design, including color schemes, visual storytelling, and visual design principles. The fourth course, Image Editing, teaches image editing skills using Adobe Photoshop. Finally, the fifth course, Photography Capstone Project, provides an opportunity to apply the skills learned in the previous courses to a real-world project, with feedback and guidance. This path is designed to be progressive, with each course building on the previous one, and to provide a solid foundation in photography and visual design.

**Learning Path for Cybersecurity, Network Defense, and Ethical Hacking**

| 3 | EDX1629 | Basic Network and Database Security | edx | Introduces network and database security, covering TCP/IP, OSI models, and network addressing. |
| 4 | EDX1034 | Network and Security Foundations | edx | Expands on EDX1629, covering network security concepts, functional and technical components of network systems, and basic security concepts. |
| 5 | EDX1624 | Network Security | edx | Develops skills in network security, including identifying attacks, collecting evidence, and testing networks for vulnerabilities. |
| 6 | EDX2560 | Jump Start: Network Security | edx | Focuses on network security, introducing the Check Point Solution, deploying security management, and creating security gateways. |
| 7 | EDX1203 | Google Cloud Computing Foundations: Networking and Security in Google Cloud | edx | Covers cloud computing, networking, and security in Google Cloud, including building secure networks and identifying cloud automation and management tools. |
| 8 | EDX2378 | Application Security for Developers | edx | Develops skills in application security, including security testing procedures, coding practices, and mitigation strategies. |
| 9 | EDX1334 | Mathematical and Computational Methods | edx | Introduces mathematical and computational methods, including calculus, geometric series, and power series expressions. |
| 10 | EDX1432 | Jump Start: Maestro Hyperscale Network Security | edx | Focuses on Maestro Hyperscale Network Security, introducing the basic components and concepts in a Maestro deployment. |
| 11 | EDX2577 | Mobile Computing with App Inventor: CS Principles Part II | edx | Covers mobile computing, app development, and network security, including designing sophisticated Android mobile apps using App Inventor. |
| 12 | EDX1919 | Introduction to Java Programming: Writing Good Code | edx | Develops skills in Java programming, including detecting and correcting common programming errors, debugging tools, and unit testing processes. |
| 13 | EDX875 | Responsible Innovation: Building Tomorrow’s Responsible Firms | edx | Focuses on responsible innovation, including developing a successful strategy for RI, embedding a safety culture, and promoting ethical leadership. |
| 14 | EDX2882 | Science, Engineering, AI & Data Ethics | edx | Covers science, engineering, AI, and data ethics, including the social and environmental impact of engineering, aspirational ethics, and preventive ethics. |
| 15 | EDX2705 | Information Technology Foundations | edx | Introduces information technology foundations, covering IT systems, software development, and network security. |
| 16 | EDX1131 | MLOps2 (AWS): Data Pipeline Automation & Optimization using Amazon Web Services | edx | Develops skills in data pipeline automation and optimization, including setting up automated monitoring and getting hands-on experience with data pipelines. |
| 17 | EDX604 | Responsible Innovation: Ethics, Safety and Technology | edx | Focuses on responsible innovation, including assessing types of innovation, assessing risks and safety, and dealing with unknown risks. |
| 18 | EDX910 | Software Defined Networking (SDN) Deployment | edx | Covers software-defined networking, including deploying SDN/NFV, applying SDN/NFV knowledge for local and global orchestration, and testing and implementing network slicing. |
| 19 | EDX478 | Circuits and Electronics 1: Basic Circuit Analysis | edx | Introduces circuits and electronics, covering circuit analysis, lumped circuit models, and abstraction. |
| 20 | EDX58 | Embedded Systems - Shape The World: Multi-Threaded Interfacing | edx | Develops skills in embedded systems, including understanding modular design and abstraction, C programming, and building and testing circuits. |
| 21 | EDX769 | Introduction to Open Source Networking Technologies | edx | Covers open-source networking technologies, including the software-defined and open-source networking landscape, disaggregated networking hardware, and open network operating systems. |
| 22 | EDX2317 | 4G Network Essentials | edx | Introduces 4G networks, covering their functioning and architecture, internal exchanges and protocols, and transport and control functions. |
| 23 | EDX3187 | Introduction to ONAP: Complete Network Automation | edx | Focuses on ONAP, covering the basics of NFV, ONAP architecture, and ONAP subprojects. |
| 24 | EDX2169 | Introduction to Cloud Infrastructure Technologies | edx | Covers cloud infrastructure technologies, including cloud computing, cloud technologies, and cloud deployment models. |
| 25 | EDX1354 | NFV Acceleration: Introduction to Anuket | edx | Develops skills in NFV acceleration, including explaining the basics of NFV, articulating the problems solved by Anuket, and describing the compliance program and related projects. |
| 26 | EDX3178 | IBM Cloud Essentials | edx | Introduces IBM Cloud Essentials, covering infrastructure services, accessing IBM Cloud, and discovering appropriate IBM Cloud services. |
| 27 | EDX890 | Embedded Systems - Shape The World: Microcontroller Input/Output | edx | Focuses on embedded systems, including understanding modular design and abstraction, C programming, and building and testing circuits. |
| 28 | EDX3026 | Ethics in AI and Data Science | edx | Covers ethics in AI and data science, including discussing the ethical challenges of AI and data science, understanding the impacts of AI and data science, and exploring the relationships between markets and data. |
| 29 | EDX1937 | Strategic Management: From Insight to Decision | edx | Develops skills in strategic management, including positioning organizations in times of transition, orchestrating strategic alliances, and assessing strategic options. |
| 30 | EDX206 | AC and Switching Circuits | edx | Introduces AC and switching circuits, covering circuit analysis, lumped circuit models, and abstraction. |
| 31 | EDX1825 | Introduction to Optimization | edx | Covers optimization, including the simplex method for linear programs, solving optimization problems in Microsoft Excel, and network flow problems. |
| 32 | EDX754 | Becoming a Hyperledger Aries Developer | edx | Develops skills in becoming a Hyperledger Aries developer, including building trust over IP (ToIP) applications, developing Aries agent code, and understanding the architecture and components of Aries agents. |
| 33 | EDX2847 | Design Practice in Business: Spark Innovation like a Designer | edx | Focuses on design practice in business, including how to approach ethical questions with respect to new technology, assessing types of innovation, and dealing with unknown risks. |
| 34 | EDX2212 | Networks, Crowds and Markets | edx | Covers networks, crowds, and markets, including using graph theory to study the Internet, social networks, and Web search, and applying game theory to analyze strategic behavior. |
| 35 | EDX1053 | Ethical Leadership in a Changing World | edx | Develops skills in ethical leadership, including understanding the meaning and importance of ethical leadership, recognizing the role of ethics in organizational decision-making, and analyzing the actions of leaders within organizations. |
| 36 | EDX270 | Tech for Good: The Role of ICT in Achieving the SDGs | edx | Covers tech for good, including how ICT can improve access to knowledge and services, promote transparency, and encourage collaboration, and how to be aware of bias in design and implementation. |
| 37 | EDX2683 | Introduction to Magma: Cloud Native Wireless Networking | edx | Introduces Magma, covering the main functions of a mobile wireless network, the key use cases and value proposition of Magma, and the overall architecture of Magma at a functional block level. |
| 38 | EDX603 | Bioethics: Proper treatment and medical research | edx | Covers bioethics, including identifying ethical issues in medicine and health sciences, providing reasonable justification for ethical decisions, and applying ethical principles of the Universal Declaration on Bioethics and Human Rights. |
| 39 | EDX477 | Ethics in Action | edx | Develops skills in ethics in action, including understanding the meaning of virtue ethics, its expression in several major religious and philosophical traditions, and the importance of establishing multi-faith consensus to advance sustainable development. |
| 40 | EDX1593 | Bridging Differences | edx | Covers bridging differences, including what it means and doesn't mean to "bridge differences," and why bridging differences is valuable to individuals and communities. |
| 41 | EDX1118 | Digital Ecosystem Infrastructure | edx | Introduces digital ecosystem infrastructure, covering cloud computing, network and application architecture, and Internet of Things (IoT) and its potential for business impact. |
| 42 | EDX2092 | Ethical Leadership: Character, Civility, and Community | edx | Develops skills in ethical leadership, including understanding the Ethical Leadership Model, narrative and dramaturgical methods in the development of character, civility, and community, and various theories and methods of ethical analysis in leadership practices. |
| 43 | EDX2181 | 5G Essentials | edx | Covers 5G essentials, including why we need 5G, 5G radio access technology, and how 5G supports Ultra Reliable Low Latency requirements. |
| 44 | EDX179 | Introduction to Lifestyle Medicine | edx | Introduces lifestyle medicine, including conceptualizing how lifestyle behaviors resulted in chronic disease in the US, and what is lifestyle medicine and its differences from traditional Western medicine. |
| 45 | EDX1042 | Valuing Diverse Perspectives in Social Work | edx | Covers valuing diverse perspectives in social work, including examining trauma and wellness through a decolonized lens, recognizing the benefits of wellness tools, and applying wellness strategies and tools. |
| 46 | EDX1329 | The Ethics of Memory | edx | Develops skills in the ethics of memory, including examining how memory was explored in 20th-century literature, law, psychoanalysis, and pop culture, and understanding why we should care about the ethical component of memory. |

The learning path for cybersecurity, network defense, and ethical hacking spans 46 periods, covering foundational and advanced topics in cybersecurity, network security, and ethical hacking. The path starts with EDX3247, "Cybersecurity: Managing Risk in the Information Age," which provides a foundational understanding of cybersecurity and risk management. The path then builds on this foundation with courses like EDX3146, "Cybersecurity Compliance and System Administration," and EDX1629, "Basic Network and Database Security," which cover compliance, regulation, and network security. The path continues with courses like EDX1034, "Network and Security Foundations," and EDX1624, "Network Security," which develop skills in network security, including threat analysis, vulnerability assessment, and penetration testing. The path also covers advanced topics like EDX2560, "Jump Start: Network Security," which focuses on network security, and EDX1203, "Google Cloud Computing Foundations: Networking and Security in Google Cloud," which covers cloud computing, networking, and security in Google Cloud. The path concludes with courses like EDX2378, "Application Security for Developers," which develops skills in application security, and EDX1334, "Mathematical and Computational Methods," which covers mathematical and computational methods in cybersecurity. Throughout the path, the learner will develop a comprehensive understanding of cybersecurity, network security, and ethical hacking, and will be able to apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios.

This learning path is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of public policy analysis and governance for a civil service career. The path starts with foundational knowledge of public policy concepts in Course 1 (COU918), followed by contextual understanding of policy analysis and governance in Course 2 (EDX3292). The path then gradually builds skills in data analysis and policy-making in Course 3 (COU3249), emphasizing critical thinking and problem-solving in policy analysis in Course 4 (EDX3263). The path continues with practical applications of policy analysis in Course 5 (COU4592), balanced cognitive load with real-world examples in Course 6 (EDX135), and advanced skill-building in policy analysis and governance in Course 7 (COU5675). The path concludes with emphasis on critical thinking and problem-solving in program management in Course 8 (EDX3287), balanced cognitive load with practical applications of data analytics and policy-making in Course 9 (COU6457), and ongoing motivation and feedback with real-world examples in Course 10 (EDX507).
